evidence_quote: The Critical Skills Employment Permit is designed to attract highly skilled people into the labour market with the aim of encouraging them to take up permanent residence in the State.

Occupations with a minimum annual remuneration of €40,904 for a restricted number of strategically important occupations contained in the Critical Skills Occupations List a relevant degree qualification or higher is required. Where the applicant has received their qualification within the 12 month period prior to the date of application for the employment permit, the minimum annual remuneration will be €36,848.
An application for any employment permit must be received at least 12 weeks before the proposed employment start date.
While the job offer must be of 2 years’ duration, the foreign national is expected to stay with the initial employer for a minimum period of 9 months.
The Immigration permission granted by the Garda National Immigration Bureau will be for 2 years, which is then renewable subject to the persons concerned meeting all relevant criteria

Permit holders can apply for immediate family reunification from the Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) of the Department of Justice and Equality and once their dependants/partners/spouses are resident in the State they are eligible to seek any employment and apply to the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment for a Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit which is currently issued free of charge.

fact_text_correction.current: The fee for a new General Employment Permit is €500 for a permit of 6 months or less, or €1,000 for permits of 6–24 months. Renewal fees are €750 (up to 6 months), €1,000 (up to 24 months), or €1,500 (up to 36 months).
fact_text_correction.corrected: The fee for a new General Employment Permit is €500 for a permit of 6 months or less, or €1,000 for permits of 6–24 months. Renewal fees are €750 (up to 6 months) or €1,500 (up to 36 months).
fact_text_correction.why: The General Employment Permit has TWO renewal tiers, not three, and the fact asserts a figure its own verified evidence_quote does not contain: that quote is the GEP table row verbatim and holds exactly four numbers — first application EUR 1,000 up to 24 months and EUR 500 for six months or less, renewal EUR 750 for six months or less and EUR 1,500 up to 36 months. No EUR 1,000 renewal appears in it. The phantom tier is traceable: the Intra-Company Transfer row, directly below GEP on the same page, genuinely does have three renewal tiers including 'EUR 1,000 up to 24 months' (see fact ict_permit_4, which states it correctly for ICT). The ICT renewal column was read onto the GEP row. Deliberately a six-word deletion and nothing else: an earlier draft of this correction also restyled the first-application half to 'up to 24 months' to match the table's phrasing, which is ambiguous beside the EUR 500 six-month band. '6-24 months' is operationally clearer and was never wrong, so it stays.
